react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on glycine, serine and threonine metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this nine-metabolite differential profile. RaMP-DB multi-DB ORA ranked KEGG:map00260 first (FDR = 1.30e-08, fold enrichment = 758), driven by L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), dihydrolipoate (KEGG:C02147), L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025), and choline (KEGG:C00114). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00260 as the top hit (p = 0.004), again anchored by L-threonine and choline. Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently returned the equivalent MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism as rank-1 (p = 0.0042, overlap = 6/6 compounds). The cross-paradigm consensus score across the three methods is compelling. Secondary convergent signals included niacinamide metabolism (KEGG:map00760, shared by RaMP and mummichog) and nitrogen metabolism (KEGG:map00910, shared by RaMP and MetaboAnalystR), each anchored by L-glutamic acid and niacinamide. L-threonine and L-glutamic acid were the strongest driver compounds, each hitting in ≥ 4 pathways across paradigms. The data suggest a treatment-induced perturbation of amino-acid interconversion and one-carbon metabolism, with secondary effects on NAD+ salvage (niacinamide) and redox cofactor regeneration (dihydrolipoate).

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260 / KEGG:hsa00260 / MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism) as the dominant biological signal in the nine-metabolite differential profile. RaMP-DB multi-DB ORA ranked this pathway first with FDR = 1.30e-08 (fold enrichment = 758), driven by four input compounds: L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), dihydrolipoate (KEGG:C02147), L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025), and choline (KEGG:C00114). Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently returned the same pathway at rank 1 with p = 0.0044 and 6/6 compound overlap. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed it as the top KEGG hit (hsa00260, p = 0.004) with choline and L-threonine as the annotated members. A secondary convergent signal in Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (KEGG:map00760 / hsa00760) appears in both RaMP (rank 8, FDR = 6.97e-04) and mummichog (rank 2, p = 0.0196), anchored by niacinamide (KEGG:C00153) and L-glutamic acid. Nitrogen metabolism (KEGG:map00910 / hsa00910) is supported by RaMP (rank 6, FDR = 6.01e-04) and MetaboAnalystR (rank 1, p = 0.0187), with L-glutamic acid and dihydrolipoate as the shared hits. L-glutamic acid is the strongest cross-pathway driver, appearing in three of the four verified pathway hits across paradigms.
